ra: The Father of Greatness heads the Realm of Light from which all Evocations proceed; apex of the Lightworld hierarchy hub. Kephalaia.
The Mother of Life, First Evocation of the Father; member of the Lightworld hierarchy. Lieu, Manichaeism in the Later Roman Empire.
Primal Man (Ohrmazd), the Father's champion evoked through the Mother of Life; core Lightworld figure of the First Creation.
The Living Spirit (Mihryazd), Evocation of the Second Creation who rescues Primal Man; member of the Lightworld hierarchy.
The Third Messenger, Evocation of the Third Creation who orchestrates liberation of the swallowed Light; member of the Lightworld hierarchy.
The Maiden of Light (Virgin of Light) accompanies the Third Messenger in the seduction of the archons; Lightworld member. Kephalaia.
Jesus the Splendour, the revealer who awakens Adam, is one of the saving Evocations of the Lightworld hierarchy.
The Column of Glory (Perfect Man / Milky Way), cosmic channel of ascending Light; a Lightworld structure within the hierarchy.
The Great Builder (Ban Rabba) constructs the New Paradise for the rescued Light; Lightworld Evocation.
The Light Mind (Nous) governs the Church and the soul of the believer; Lightworld member. Kephalaia ch. 38.
King of Glory, one of the Five Sons of the Living Spirit governing the cosmic apparatus; Lightworld hierarchy member.
King of Honour, one of the Five Sons of the Living Spirit, watcher over the heavens; Lightworld member.
Adamas of Light, a Son of the Living Spirit who combats the dark powers; Lightworld member.
The Five Sons of Primal Man (the Light elements / soul-armour) deployed and swallowed in the cosmic battle; Lightworld collective member.
Call and Answer, paired Lightworld hypostases mediating the rescue of Primal Man; members of the hierarchy.
The Porter (Splenditenens / Omophoros), one of the Five Sons of the Living Spirit who supports the cosmos; Lightworld member.
Keeper of Splendour, one of the Five Sons of the Living Spirit; Lightworld member of the second-creation hierarchy.
The Last Statue (Andrias), the eschatological assembling of redeemed Light at the consummation; Lightworld figure of the hierarchy. Kephalaia.
The dispersed Light particles (the suffering Living Self) are of the substance of the Realm of Light; grouped structurally under the Lightworld hub.
The Twin (Syzygos), Mani's heavenly counterpart mediating revelation; Lightworld member. Cologne Mani Codex.
The Friend of the Lights, an early Evocation of the second-creation series; Lightworld member. Theodore bar Konai.
First Evocation: the Father of Greatness evokes the Mother of Life. Standard three-evocation cosmogony in the Kephalaia and Theodore bar Konai's summary.
The Mother of Life evokes Primal Man (Ohrmazd) as the Father's warrior against Darkness; second link of the First Creation chain.
Primal Man is called the son of the Mother of Life in the Psalm-Book and Kephalaia; filial language of the first Evocation series.
Second Creation: in response to Primal Man's prayer the Father (with the Mother of Life) evokes the Living Spirit to descend and rescue him. Lieu.
The Five Sons (the five Light elements / soul-armour: Air, Wind, Light, Water, Fire) are the sons Primal Man arms himself with and offers to the Darkness. Theodore bar Konai.
The Maiden of Light is evoked with the Third Messenger and displayed to the archons to release the Light through the seduction of the rulers. Theodore bar Konai.
The Column of Glory, ascending channel of liberated Light, is established within the third-creation apparatus deployed by the Third Messenger. Kephalaia.
Jesus the Splendour is sent in the wake of the Third Messenger to awaken Adam and reveal gnosis; among the later Evocations of the saving sequence. Lieu; Kephalaia.
The Light Mind (the Great Nous) proceeds from Jesus the Splendour to organize the Church and indwell the elect. Kephalaia ch. 38 ('On the Light Mind').
The Great Builder constructs the New Earth / New Paradise as a repository for the rescued Light, an extension of the World of Light. Lieu.
The Porter upholds the cosmos fashioned by the Living Spirit from the bodies of the defeated archons, the apparatus that filters Light back toward the World of Light.
The Father of Greatness dwells in the Realm/World of Light with the aeons; standard Manichaean topography. Kephalaia; Psalm-Book.
At the end the Last Statue gathers the last salvageable Light and ascends to the World of Light, sealing the separation of the two natures. Lieu.
The Light Particles (the soul / Living Self mixed into matter) are the object of rescue accomplished through the Third Messenger's evocations. Kephalaia.
Mani received his revelation through his heavenly Twin, identified with the syzygos sent by Jesus the Splendour / the Paraclete; Mani's apostolate continues the saving revelation. Cologne Mani Codex.
The Twin (Syzygos / al-Tawm), Mani's divine counterpart who delivers the revelation, is associated with the saving emanation of Jesus the Splendour / the Light Mind. Cologne Mani Codex.
The Five Worlds of Darkness stand in eternal opposition to the World of Light; the two-principle dualism foundational to Manichaeism. Kephalaia.
The Archons (rulers/abortions of darkness) are subordinate powers of the realm ruled by the King of Darkness. Lieu.
The Demons are denizens of the Five Worlds of Darkness, offspring of the dark elements. Kephalaia.
Az, the demoness of concupiscence/greed who drives the propagation of bodies to keep Light imprisoned, belongs to the powers of darkness. Middle Persian Manichaean texts; Lieu.
Matter is the dark principle that imprisons and opposes the Light particles; the central soteriological conflict of mixing. Kephalaia; Psalm-Book.
Jesus patibilis (suffering, immanent Light) and Jesus the Splendour (transcendent revealer) are two aspects of the multiple Manichaean Jesus-figure; aligned as facets of the same name. Lieu.

Cross-tradition typological parallel: the Manichaean World/Realm of Light and the Mandaean World of Light (alma d-nhura) are cognate Mesopotamian gnostic light-realm concepts; aligned (not identical). Note homonym/parallel for reviewer. Lieu; Buckley, The Mandaeans.

Cross-tradition typological parallel: the Manichaean realm/King of Darkness corresponds to the Mandaean World of Darkness as cognate dualist counter-realms in the shared Mesopotamian gnostic milieu. Buckley; Lieu.
